title: 十一月四日风雨大作·其二
titlePy: Shíyī Yuè Sì Rì Fēng Yǔ Dà Zuò
titleEn: A Great Storm on the Fourth Day of the Eleventh Month (No. 2)
author: 陆游
intro: An old man lies in bed in a lonely village, too frail to get up — yet still dreams of guarding the frontier. On a stormy night the wind and rain turn, in his dream, into armoured horses crossing frozen rivers.
analysis: 这首诗写于陆游六十八岁时，他已经退居家乡山阴多年，生活清苦，身体也不好。一、二句是自述：我直挺挺地躺在孤零零的村子里，却不为自己悲哀，还想着为国家去守卫边疆。“轮台”是汉代西域的地名，这里泛指边关。“僵卧”和“尚思”形成强烈对比：身体老了、动不了，心却还年轻。三、四句写夜深了，躺着听外面的风雨声，听着听着睡着了，梦里披着铁甲的战马正跨过结冰的河流去作战。风雨声和战马奔腾的声音连在一起，现实与梦境自然衔接。“铁马冰河入梦来”写出了一个老人至死不变的报国之心，成了陆游最有名的诗句之一。
analysisEn: Lu You wrote this at sixty-seven, after years of retirement in his home village near Shaoxing, poor and in poor health. The first two lines are a self-portrait: I lie stiff in bed in a lonely village, but I do not pity myself — I still dream of guarding the frontier for my country. Luntai was a Han-dynasty outpost in the far west, used here to mean any border post. Notice the contrast between 僵卧 (“lying stiff”) and 尚思 (“still thinking of”): the body is old and stuck, the heart is still young. In the last two lines the night is late; he lies listening to the wind driving the rain, and drifts off. In his dream, armoured horses are crossing frozen rivers into battle. The roar of the storm outside slides into the thunder of hooves, so reality and dream join without a seam. The final line, 铁马冰河入梦来, has become one of Lu You’s best-known: the picture of an old man whose wish to serve his country never fades, even in sleep. This is the second of two poems with the same title; the first describes the storm itself.
background: Lu You (1125–1210) spent his life urging the Southern Song court to win back the north from the Jin. He wrote this in the winter of 1192, living in retirement at Shanyin (today’s Shaoxing).
pronunciation: 为国 wèi；戍 shù；夜阑 lán；僵卧 jiāng wò。
version: 采用通行教材文本（统编教材七年级上册，题为《十一月四日风雨大作（其二）》）。原作共两首，网站选第二首。

lines.py: jiāng wò gū cūn bù zì āi
lines.lit: Lying stiff in a lonely village, I do not grieve for myself;
lines.en: Stiff in my bed in a lonely village, I don’t feel sorry for myself —

lines.py: shàng sī wèi guó shù lún tái
lines.lit: I still think of guarding Luntai for my country.
lines.en: I still long to stand guard at the frontier.

lines.py: yè lán wò tīng fēng chuī yǔ
lines.lit: Late at night, lying, I hear the wind blowing the rain;
lines.en: Deep in the night I lie and hear the wind lash the rain,

lines.py: tiě mǎ bīng hé rù mèng lái
lines.lit: iron horses and frozen rivers come into my dream.
lines.en: and armoured horses on frozen rivers gallop into my dreams.

words.en: to lie stiff (from age or illness)
words.note: 僵：僵硬，现代汉语“冻僵”“僵硬”。
现代汉语说“自怜”“为自己难过”。

words.en: Luntai, a Han-dynasty frontier post in the west
words.note: 在今新疆，这里泛指边疆。
阑：将尽。现代汉语“夜阑人静”。
现代汉语“金戈铁马”形容战争。
这里指北方结冰的河；今天“冰河”也指冰川。

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 风雨大作是真实的天气，也像战场上的厮杀声，把诗人带进梦里。
imagery.en: The raging wind is real weather — and the din of battle that carries him into his dream.

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 冬夜冷雨写出孤村的凄清，也唤起他对征战的回忆。
imagery.en: Cold winter rain shows how bleak the village is, and stirs memories of campaigning.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 梦中的铁马是他想上战场、收复失地的愿望。
imagery.en: The armoured horses of his dream are his wish to ride to war and win back the lost north.
